limitations: The local TRAIN log-count center can become stale: frozen-predictor class-reallocation development diagnostics reverse the prior-center advantage. This is a boundary observation, not evidence that an adaptation works.
The isotropic quadratic treats log frequencies with very different count uncertainty equally; the completed scalar-lambda scan does not test anisotropic count-derived geometry.

The current evidence does not separate local prior information from class evidence already present in frozen logits; apparent benefit can reflect shrinkage, label-shift correction or representation error compensation.
Twenty stored coordinates do not establish that every class-specific scale needs to be fitted when local TRAIN omits classes; BCTS and matched-capacity controls remain important rivals.
Existing results concern label-skew clients and limited partition realizations, not arbitrary non-IID or feature-shift robustness; running new partitions must not be anticipated.

Generic personalized regularization centers are established in PRIOR/pFedBreD. A contribution needs a specific output-space mechanism, an explicit compact budget and attribution controls; unresolved LaSCal/FedNPC overlap remains unresolved.
